campaign.note: summed per run across the campaign window since the marker. NOT the live panel, which is this run only — a campaign sum and a run counter are different quantities and the panel publishes exactly one of them

unit: reference unit — i7-12700, DeckLink Duo 2, free-running. Output is 1080p50 SDI; the test schedule is deliberately mixed-source — 25i · 25p · 29.97p · 50p · 50i across DNxHD, H.264, MPEG-2, ProRes — so junctions cross format families every pass. A development bench running a test schedule, not a production fleet.

figures.label: Soak elapsed
figures.provenance: soak sampler silent — figures withheld rather than frozen

figures.label: Frames delivered
figures.provenance: engine unreachable and soak log unreadable

figures.label: Late frames
figures.provenance: the ENGINE's count of clock wakes that arrived more than 500 µs behind the instant they were scheduled for. An internal timing miss, not a lost frame — the frame is still built, and the card's output buffer absorbs the delay. This run; it resets at a restart, and so does the frame count above it, so the two always share a scope

figures.label: Card-reported late frames
figures.provenance: the CARD's own counter, not the engine's — an independent instrument on the far side of the handoff. Nothing reached the SDI output late

figures.label: Frame underruns
figures.provenance: cumulative since engine start. A standing value of a few hundred is decoder start-up priming, present at every start by design — growth after start-up is what would indicate a fault

figures.label: Clock phase, worst this run
figures.provenance: worst single tick since this run began, never reset. The ceiling pre-registered for this campaign, frozen before it started, is 2,000,000 ns — one tenth of a frame

figures.label: Clock phase, typical
figures.provenance: mean magnitude — not the signed mean, which cancels

figures.label: Card crystal error vs TAI
figures.provenance: measured continuously; the figure the drift compensation is built on

figures.label: Frames shed by drift compensation
figures.provenance: surplus frames discarded from the handoff queue, by design

historical.label: Longest continuous engine run
historical.provenance: one unbroken run, 2026-08-06T19:53:26Z to 2026-08-20T23:16:43Z, ended deliberately at the close of the 14-day campaign. Derived three independent ways that agree to within twenty seconds — one part in 61,000: the supervisor reports NRestarts=0 across the whole span (339.3881 h), the engine's own frame counter reached 61,088,850 at 50 fps (339.3825 h, read 14 s before the stop), and the 1 Hz diagnostic line spans 339.3861 h. Rounded DOWN to whole hours — a final figure, not a floor

historical.label: Frames delivered, that run
historical.provenance: the engine's own frame counter 14 s before it was stopped; at 50 fps it is one of the three derivations of the 339 h above, agreeing with the supervisor span to within twenty seconds. Frames PRODUCED by the engine, which is not the same as frames the card put on the wire — 214 were shed to drift compensation, by design

historical.label: Late SDI frames, that run
historical.provenance: reported by the card itself, not by us: frames that reached the SDI output late. Zero, across 339 hours — and the denominator is the card's own, not the engine's 61,088,850 produced, because 214 of those were shed to drift compensation before the card saw them

historical.label: Late engine frames, that run
historical.provenance: a different counter answering a different question — twice in 339 hours the clock thread woke more than half a millisecond late. The frame was still built and the card's buffer absorbed it, which is what the row above independently confirms. Published because the campaign's frozen criterion allowed ZERO of these, so it failed its own test, and a criterion you only quote when it passes is not a criterion

historical.label: Clock phase, median tick
historical.provenance: the worst tick in each second, then the spread of those across all 1,221,791 seconds of the run: median 197 ns, p90 735, p99 1,059, p99.9 1,219, p99.99 39,780, worst 569,759. Half the run sat inside 197 ns and 99.9 % of it inside 1.22 µs. Published as a distribution because a latched maximum is the least representative number a run produces, and quoting it alone flatters nobody honestly

historical.label: Worst single tick, that run
historical.provenance: latched maximum, never reset — under 3 % of one 20 ms frame, and the tail of the distribution in the row above rather than its shape. It belongs to a population of 109 excursions of 380 µs or more across the fortnight, all in the same direction; cause open and under investigation

historical.label: Clip junctions, that run
historical.provenance: every transition between schedule items, taken from the as-run log and checked against the house tick grid: 7,439, and every one of them frame-exact — the interval between the last frame of the outgoing item and the first frame of the incoming one was exactly one source frame, worst deviation 79 ns. No gaps, no overlaps. One further transition is deliberately not counted as a junction: the 48.6 s gap at the very start, where this run itself began

historical.label: Seconds at exactly 50 frames, that run
historical.provenance: every second of the run — and there are no missing seconds, because 1,221,791 diagnostic seconds span exactly 1,221,791 seconds of wall clock. In all 1,221,790 intervals between them the frame counter advanced by exactly 50 and the timecode by exactly one second, across 14 midnights, with the clock reporting LOCK in every one

historical.label: Compliance records dropped, that run
historical.provenance: the as-run writer hands records to a queue that is allowed to drop its newest entry rather than stall the clock thread, and writes an exception into the chain when it does. It never did: zero drops across the run's 47,518,115 records. Published as a zero only because the thing that would have made it non-zero leaves its own evidence — an unwitnessed zero is what this panel withdrew a row over on 4 Aug

historical.label: As-run records checked for tampering
historical.provenance: every record in the archive, re-checked after the 14-day run: 47 day files, 120,483,920 records, 13 chain segments. One broken boundary, 20→21 June 2026, known and pre-dating this run — it is a real finding and it is why the archive reads INVALID rather than clean. No other break, and 0 false positives across the rest; six forgery vectors closed
